purpose: Spoiler-free authoring-to-engine acceptance cases. Placeholder ids and text only. This is a contract, not evidence of runtime passing.

publicOutcome.text: The confirmed action changes the visible situation.

ending.costNotice: Continuing closes other routes in this world. Confirm?

tests.given: A world has startSceneId pointing to an existing scene.
tests.when: A new isolated session is initialized.
expect: Server selects the declared starting scene, not a model guess.
Only authorized public scene text is exposed.

tests.given: An event stores publicOutcome as an object with text and authorization metadata.
tests.when: The event is not committed, then is committed once.
expect: Before commit, neither text nor hidden condition is exposed.
After commit, only authorized text/facts are available to player narration.
The player response never includes private conditions, effect targets or internal identifiers.

tests.given: A placeholder event uses dialogue_choice_committed with choiceId and npcId.
tests.when: Player discusses a choice, then explicitly commits it.
expect: Discussion and ASK do not mutate NPC relationship.
Only a real committed choice can trigger the event.
Replayed commit does not apply relationship twice.

tests.given: A set_flag effect causes a world_flag_changed event.
tests.when: The source action commits.
expect: Dependent flag event is evaluated only after the first change is committed.
The same source cannot generate infinite flag-trigger recursion.
A repeated action id cannot duplicate the public result.

tests.given: Scene choices list a valid next scene and an event listens for scene_entered.
tests.when: Player previews a route, then commits the selected route.
expect: Listing choices does not advance scene.
A committed, validated transition advances once.
The destination scene_entered event fires once after transition.

tests.given: An event lists revealsFacts and publicOutcome.authorizedFactIds.
tests.when: Narrator mentions a fact before commit, then the server commits an authorized reveal.
expect: Narrator text alone never grants a fact.
Only the server-confirmed reveal updates player-known facts.
No unrelated or future fact is included in the public result.

tests.given: A content package uses a trigger, effect, or outcome shape not supported by the runtime.
tests.when: A preflight compatibility check runs.
expect: Import is rejected or explicitly blocked with a non-spoiler diagnostic.
The runtime must not silently ignore required events and report the package playable.
Diagnostics contain counts/codes, never secret ids or story text.

tests.given: A terminal destination has an ending id, public costNotice and satisfied entryRequirements.
tests.when: The player inspects or selects that destination but has not separately confirmed.
expect: Show only the truthful public costNotice; do not expose private conditions.
Do not set ending_locked, move into the terminal scene, or spend resources.
A generic Continue or a preview must not count as explicit ending consent.

tests.given: One player saw the costNotice for ending-demo-a in session A at world version V.
tests.when: A confirmation arrives from another session, a changed target or a later world version.
expect: Reject the stale or mismatched confirmation without changing world state.
Allow a new spoiler-free preview and fresh explicit confirmation.
No hidden flags or private ids appear in the player error.

tests.given: A terminal scene has unsatisfied entryRequirements.
tests.when: The player attempts direct travel, event advance_scene or repeated commit.
expect: Every path is blocked by server-owned preconditions.
Narration, ASK and a model-suggested plan cannot bypass the gate.
The response is in-world and does not expose secret requirement details.

tests.given: The player explicitly confirms an eligible terminal route and its event locks ending_locked.
tests.when: The commit succeeds, repeats with the same id, then another ending is attempted.
expect: The first commit applies ending effects and lock atomically exactly once.
Same-id replay returns the original result without duplicate consequence.
Conflicting ending lock rejects the entire new event with no partial application.

tests.given: A player has validated MATH 1920 evidence but declines the offered ending.
tests.when: They choose to explore, ask questions or pursue another viable route.
expect: Declining the ending changes neither committed world state nor learning evidence.
The DM continues the story without a forced quiz or automatic ending.
Later commitment still requires a fresh appropriate notice and explicit confirmation.

tests.given: A placeholder bundle contains a missing costNotice, duplicate ending id, eager scene-entry lock, missing lock event, unsupported entryRequirements or invalid stateEffects.
tests.when: Authoring preflight validates the bundle.
expect: Each unsafe category is a blocking error rather than a silent skip.
Diagnostic output contains only error category and count, not private ids, values or prose.
A static missing grant path for remove_item is a warning, not automatically a blocking error.

tests.given: A public costNotice is available before an irreversible choice.
tests.when: The DM describes the stakes and the player asks for more detail.
expect: DM explains the known consequence without inventing facts or revealing future plot.
The player may decline and continue exploring without mutation.
Math knowledge may support decision-making but never replaces explicit consent.

tests.given: An eligible ending has been previewed and then successfully committed with its matching terminal lock event.
tests.when: The server creates the next-chapter opening snapshot.
expect: Capture only after the ending lock and associated terminal effects are committed.
Bind snapshot to the successful ending commit and source content revision.
A preview, decline or failed ending attempt produces no snapshot.

tests.given: An ending commit has already produced an immutable snapshot.
tests.when: The same commit is retried and a conflicting ending is attempted.
expect: The retry resolves to the original snapshot identity without duplicating consequences.
A conflicting ending cannot replace the source ending or rewrite the snapshot.
No old inventory grant or learning reward is applied again.

tests.given: The DM mentioned a plausible fact, but only a different fact has a committed discovery event.
tests.when: The snapshot is constructed.
expect: Include only server-confirmed facts with originating event and audience scope.
Exclude narrator conjecture, uncommitted dialogue and unverified clues.
The next chapter must not treat an NPC's heard claim as a confirmed world fact.

tests.given: A placeholder NPC has a heard claim, a belief and separately confirmed knowledge.
tests.when: NPC continuity is transferred and later summarized for the player.
expect: Preserve each NPC memory layer separately with its provenance.
Private belief and private knowledge are excluded from player-visible summaries.
Relationship history is not overwritten by the latest narration tone.

tests.given: A server-private snapshot contains a hidden thread and an authorized player fact.
tests.when: The next chapter requests an opening narration view.
expect: Only authorized facts, visible item ownership and eligible consequence summaries enter the DM's player-facing context.
Internal ids, hidden threads, NPC private knowledge and future plot are never exposed.
The narrator cannot infer a solution from the ending reference.

tests.given: The previous world contains one confirmed MATH 1920 learning evidence reference and one assisted unverified answer.
tests.when: The next chapter opens.
expect: Carry forward verified evidence by reference and preserve its verification status.
Do not promote the assisted answer into independent mastery.
Do not mint a new reward or replay a spent bonus merely because the evidence was carried forward.

tests.given: A snapshot request references a stale source world revision or a terminal scene without a matching committed ending lock.
tests.when: A new chapter attempts to resume from it.
expect: Reject the snapshot as an authoritative opening state without partial transfer.
Do not guess a default ending, invent missing facts or expose private diagnostics.
Return a recoverable server-side error path for the engine owner to handle.

integrationNotes: The authoring source may keep structured publicOutcome metadata; an adapter may produce a runtime string only after preserving authorization semantics.
change_npc_relation.value is a string relation band, not a numeric delta.
The first-world authoring graph has scene choices; choices alone are not proof that the runtime has committed a transition.
No formal story content, hidden identities, puzzle answers or actual world ids are included.
Do not mark these cases passed until run against an isolated server with placeholder content.
Ending semantics and preflight cases are design contracts only; current runtime behavior and test execution are unverified.
Chapter-opening continuity snapshot cases are proposed narrative acceptance contracts, not a runtime implementation or executed tests.
